about: Simplified Technical English wording for the factor table, the power and steady influences, and the environment figures (site/data factors.json, extra.json, extra-prose.json, environment.json).

factors.json.Pits, caves and skylights: dropped by th: The table has no row for pits, caves and skylights, because the team lead removed them.
factors.json.These are parts of the problem of findin: These figures are parts of the problem of navigation by sight. We do not give one score for them.
factors.json.A coarse grid value is the value of a bo: A value from a coarse grid is the value of a box that is much larger than the area. It is not a measurement at the place.
factors.json.New factors for this area, each tagged b: New factors for this area. Each figure has a tag for its kind. If we have a figure for the lunar region, the card shows it also.
factors.json.Ice-free ground in Antarctica is permafr: The literature says that all ice-free ground in Antarctica is permafrost. The permafrost map does not include Antarctica.
factors.json.A count of catalogued events, not a meas: This is a count of catalogued events, not a measurement of ground motion at the place, and not a hazard map. Only a seismometer at the place gives a real test. The networks of seismometers increased during the 16 years. In some places, for example the Kobuk valley, the later years have several times as many events a year as the early years. Thus, the early years show too few events, and the number of years with events can be too low. Distances are from the centre of the place.
factors.json.Cannot tell: the catalogue does not reco: Cannot tell: the catalogue does not record small tremors here. Thus, an empty circle around the place does not show that there are no small tremors.
factors.json.Factors already on the page's own card a: This part does not repeat the factors that are on the place card already.
factors.json.Measured (or computed from measured data: Measured, or calculated from measured data, and part of the score that puts the lists in order.
factors.json.Read from a measured map, a catalogue or: Read from a measured map, a catalogue or a model grid, and shown for each place. It is not part of the score.
factors.json.A word set by a stated rule of our own f: A word that our own stated rule sets from other layers. It is not a measurement.
factors.json.We hold figures for the lunar regions or: We have figures for the lunar regions or the Mars sites, but not for the places on Earth.
factors.json.Another member is still writing the inpu: Another member of the team did not complete the input file yet.
There is no figure. The table gives the reason.
factors.json.measured from a map, a catalogue or the: measured from a map, a catalogue or the calculated path of the Sun, for the area itself
factors.json.a value of a grid box much larger than t: a value of a grid box that is much larger than the area, not a measurement at the place
factors.json.a word set by our own stated rule; not a: a word that our own stated rule sets, not a measurement
The Mars part does not use it.
Our data has no figure for Mars.
We did not make this figure.
factors.json.Hours a year in spells of 2 h or more wi: The hours in a year when the centre of the Sun is above the horizon but below the Sun ceiling of the lunar region. Only spells of 2 h or more count.
factors.json.Not sunshine under cloud, and not the Su: It is not the sunshine below cloud, and it is not the height of the Sun at one moment.
factors.json.The Sun's path computed every minute for: We calculated the path of the Sun at each minute for each area, first over a flat horizon, then over the real hills.
factors.json.The Sun ceiling at each lunar region fro: We calculated the Sun ceiling of each lunar region from its latitude and the 1.54 degree tilt of the Moon.
factors.json.Not used in the Mars part, which compare: The Mars part does not use it. That part compares climate and ground, not low Sun.
factors.json.Mean cloud amount by month for the 1 deg: The mean cloud amount for each month in the 1 degree box that holds the area. Step 4 keeps the hours that remain under typical cloud.
factors.json.Not the cloud at the low-Sun hours thems: It is not the cloud during the hours of low Sun, and it is not a measurement at the area.
The Moon has no air and no cloud.
factors.json.Step 4 of the map takes typical cloud ou: Step 4 of the map removes the hours that typical cloud hides. The scores that put the lists in order do not use it.
factors.json.The UV index at the ground under the rea: The mean UV index at the ground for each month, below the real sky, over all 24 hours of the day.
factors.json.Not the noon UV index of a weather forec: It is not the noon UV index of a weather forecast, and it is not a measurement at the place.
factors.json.No air or ozone on the Moon to filter UV: The Moon has no air or ozone to filter UV. Our data has no UV figure for the Moon.
Our data has no UV figure for Mars.
factors.json.Sunlight reaching level ground in a mean: The sunlight that gets to level ground in a mean day of each month, below the real mix of cloud and clear sky. The night is included.
factors.json.Not the light on a tilted panel, and not: It is not the light on a tilted panel, and it is not a measurement at the place.
factors.json.The lunar regions' lit share of all time: The share of all time that the lunar regions are in sunlight, from the PGDA illumination maps. Our data does not have the energy for each day.
factors.json.Sunlight at the top of the Mars atmosphe: The NASA fact sheet gives the sunlight at the top of the Mars atmosphere.
factors.json.Days with daytime cloud under 10 percent: The days in a typical year (2001 to 2020) when the daytime cloud in the 1 degree box is less than 10 percent.
factors.json.Not days of clear sky during the low-Sun: It is not the days of clear sky during the hours of low Sun, and it is not a count at the place.
factors.json.Every day is clear on the Moon: there is: Each day is clear on the Moon, because there is no air.
factors.json.How much the air's dust, smoke and haze: How much the dust, smoke and haze in the air decrease the light of the Sun. The figure is the aerosol optical depth of the 1 degree box.
factors.json.Not dust on the ground, and not dust alo: It is not the dust on the ground. It is not dust only, but all aerosol together.
factors.json.NASA POWER climatology AOD_55_ADJ for th: NASA POWER climatology AOD_55_ADJ for the areas and AOD_55 for the Mars squares. The service has no figure for dust only.
factors.json.No air on the Moon, so no haze; lunar du: The Moon has no air, thus it has no haze. Lunar dust is on the ground.
Martinez et al. 2017 describe the dusty sky of Mars in words only.
factors.json.The real horizon of each area from a 60: The real horizon of each area, from a 60 m height model. It removes the hours of low Sun that the hills hide.
It is not the shade from plants or buildings.
factors.json.The lunar regions' 5 m LOLA models (PGDA: The 5 m LOLA models of the lunar regions (PGDA product 78).
factors.json.Not the slope under one footprint: 90 m: It is not the slope below one footprint. The 90 m pixels remove small steps in the ground.
factors.json.Copernicus DEM GLO-90; Mars squares: slo: Copernicus DEM GLO-90. For the Mars squares: slopes across approximately 3.7 km.
factors.json.How much the area's spread of slopes ove: How much the distribution of slopes in the area overlaps the distribution of slopes in the lunar region.
factors.json.Not a match of single landforms, and bli: It does not compare single landforms, and it cannot see features smaller than 90 m.
factors.json.How bumpy the ground is once the local s: How rough the ground is after we remove the local slope, at baselines of 90, 270 and 810 m.
factors.json.Not boulders: nothing under 90 m is seen: It does not show boulders, because on Earth the model cannot see features smaller than 90 m. GLO-90 includes forest and buildings.
factors.json.Not worked out for the Mars squares: the: We did not calculate it for the Mars squares, because their heights are 1.85 km apart.
factors.json.Plain, rolling ground, hills or mountain: Plain, rolling ground, hills or mountains. Limits on slope and relief set the class, after Hammond (1964).
factors.json.Not a geomorphological map, and not chec: It is not a geomorphological map. Nobody checked it in the field.
factors.json.Copernicus DEM GLO-90 window; Mars squar: A Copernicus DEM GLO-90 window. For the Mars squares: a relief class only.
factors.json.The same rule on 10 km pieces of the 5 m: The same rule, used on 10 km pieces of the 5 m LOLA models.
factors.json.Shown as its parts side by side: the Sun: The page shows its four parts next to each other. The parts are the height of the Sun, the share of ground in terrain shadow, the roughness at 90 m and the haze.
It is not one score. We do not give a score.
factors.json.The parts' own sources (Sun path, horizo: The sources of each part (Sun path, horizons, GLO-90, NASA POWER aerosol).
factors.json.The lunar regions' Sun ceiling, lit shar: The Sun ceiling, the lit share and the roughness of the lunar regions.
We did not make it for the Mars part.
factors.json.The share of the area's land that is bar: The share of the land in the area that is bare rock, gravel or sand, without plants or permanent ice.
factors.json.Not snow-free in every season: snow is a: It does not mean that the ground is free of snow in each season. Snow is a separate step.
factors.json.Not measured in the south, where the roc: We did not measure it in the south. There, the page uses the rock season.
factors.json.Not used in the Mars part; it uses tempe: The Mars part does not use it. It uses temperature and dryness.
factors.json.Whether the area lies on a listed anorth: This tells if the area is on a listed body of anorthosite, the rock of the bright highlands of the Moon.
factors.json.Not a rock map of the area: a listed bod: It is not a rock map of the area. Each listed body is a circle around its published centre.
The Mars squares that are on a listed body.
factors.json.The share of sunlight the ground reflect: The share of sunlight that the ground reflects, as a mean of the sunlit months of the year, for a 1 degree box.
factors.json.Not the brightness of bare rock: the box: It is not the brightness of bare rock, because the box contains a mix of snow, sea and plants.
We did not read a file of lunar albedo for this version of the page.
factors.json.Whether the main rock of the half-degree: This tells if the main rock of the half-degree box is volcanic, and if it is like basalt (basic volcanic).
factors.json.Not the rock at the place: only the main: It is not the rock at the place. It is only the main rock of a box of approximately 55 km.
Our data has no rock class for each Mars site.
factors.json.The usual minerals of the area's mapped: The usual minerals of the mapped rock class of the area, from one table that we made. The table also tells how much they are like the Moon and Mars.
We read it from a rock map, not from spectra.
Our data has no mineral figure for each Mars site.
factors.json.Which silicate minerals lead (plagioclas: Which silicate minerals are the main ones (plagioclase, pyroxene and olivine, quartz). We read them from the mineral family.
factors.json.Not a chemical analysis: no element or o: It is not a chemical analysis. We did not read a figure for an element or an oxide.
We use the row for the mineral family in its place.
Our data has no figure for each Mars site.
factors.json.How closely the ground's reflected spect: How closely the spectrum that the ground reflects matches the spectra of the Moon or Mars.
factors.json.No spectra of Earth places or of the lun: We did not read spectra of places on Earth or of the lunar regions for this version of the page. We use the row for the mineral family in its place.
factors.json.How fast the ground heats and cools: our: How fast the ground heats and cools. Our index is (1 - albedo) divided by the daily swing of air temperature. We divide the places into thirds by this index.
factors.json.Not thermal inertia: an index from coars: It is not thermal inertia. It is an index from coarse climate grids.
factors.json.No Diviner polar thermal-inertia product: There is no Diviner product for thermal inertia at the poles.
factors.json.Whether ilmenite-bearing rock (the oxyge: This tells if rock with ilmenite (the oxygen ore in lunar plans) is possible, from the mapped rock class.
It is not an ore survey. It gives no assay and no grade.
factors.json.Rockiness: our word from bare share, ste: Rockiness: a word that we set from the bare share, steep or rough ground and loose sediment. We use it in place of rock abundance.
factors.json.Not a count of rocks or boulders: 90 m h: It is not a count of rocks or boulders. Heights at intervals of 90 m cannot show single rocks.
factors.json.The Diviner rock map stops at 80 S; all: The Diviner rock map stops at 80 S. All the lunar regions are farther south.
factors.json.No numeric Mars rock-abundance file was: We did not find a file of numbers for rock abundance on Mars.
factors.json.Ground that changes by itself today: mov: Ground that changes by itself today, for example dunes that move, streaks on slopes and frost.
factors.json.The Gale rate is the dune field's, not t: The rate at Gale is the rate of the dune field, not of the landing point.
There is no figure for each area.
factors.json.About 1 m a year of dune advance at Gale: At Gale, the dunes move approximately 1 m a year (NASA APOD).
factors.json.No per-place Earth figure; figures exist: There is no figure for each place on Earth. There are figures for the lunar regions or the Mars sites.
factors.json.Mean air temperature 2 m above the groun: The mean air temperature 2 m above the ground for each month, at the nearest grid point.
factors.json.Not the ground surface temperature, and: It is not the temperature of the ground surface, and it is not a measurement at the place.
factors.json.The day's warmest hour minus its coldest: The temperature of the warmest hour of the day minus the temperature of the coldest hour, for air 2 m above the ground. It is a mean for each month.
factors.json.Not the swing of the ground surface, and: It is not the swing at the ground surface, and it is not a measurement at the place.
factors.json.Diviner polar tables were too large to r: The Diviner polar tables were too large to read for this version of the page.
factors.json.Mean wind speed 10 m above the ground ov: The mean wind speed 10 m above the ground for all hours, at the nearest grid point.
factors.json.Not gusts and not valley winds smaller t: It does not show gusts, or valley winds that are smaller than the grid box.
The Moon has no air and no wind.
Our data has no wind figure for Mars.
factors.json.Wetness of the top 5 cm of soil, from 0: The wetness of the top 5 cm of soil, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated), from a land model.
factors.json.Not a probe measurement. A value of 1 al: It is not a measurement with a probe. If the value is 1 all year, the grid point of the model is ice.
Lunar soil contains no liquid water.
factors.json.No liquid water at the surface; see near: There is no liquid water at the surface. See near-surface water.
factors.json.The modelled probability of permafrost,: The probability of permafrost from a model, as a mean of the 1 km pixels in the area, and the permafrost zone.
factors.json.Not a measurement in the ground. Antarct: It is not a measurement in the ground. This map does not include Antarctica.
factors.json.Lunar polar ground is frozen all year; s: The polar ground of the Moon is frozen all year. See depth to stable ice.
factors.json.Mars ice depth at the sites; see depth t: The depth of ice at the Mars sites. See depth to stable ice.
factors.json.How far down frozen ground or stable ice: The depth at which frozen ground or stable ice starts. On Earth, our rule sets a class from the permafrost zone.
On Earth, it is not a measurement of the depth of thaw.
factors.json.Our rule on the permafrost zone; no metr: Our rule, used on the permafrost zone. We did not find depths in metres.
factors.json.Phoenix 3 to 5 cm by digging; published: Phoenix: 3 to 5 cm, from the trench that the lander dug. Arcadia and Deuteronilus: published words.
factors.json.Earth: top-soil water and ground ice by: On Earth, our rule sets classes for water in the top soil and for ground ice. On the Moon and Mars, instruments in orbit measure hydrogen.
factors.json.Not an orbital hydrogen measurement on E: On Earth, it is not a measurement of hydrogen from orbit. The figures for the Moon and Mars are for a region, not for the landing point.
factors.json.Catalogued earthquakes of magnitude 5 or: The catalogued earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more within 200 km from 1990 to 2025, with the largest one and the nearest one.
It is not a hazard map, and it is not a forecast.
factors.json.NASA 2024 release on south-polar moonqua: A NASA release from 2024 about moonquakes near the south pole, in words only.
factors.json.InSight's 1,319 marsquakes for the whole: The 1,319 marsquakes that InSight recorded for the whole planet.
factors.json.Catalogued events of magnitude 1 to unde: The catalogued events of magnitude 1 to less than 5 within 100 km, from 2010 to 2025. It also tells if the catalogue can see them here.
factors.json.Not ground motion at the place; where th: It is not the ground motion at the place. If the network has few stations, the answer is 'cannot tell'.
factors.json.No seismometer has worked near the south: No seismometer worked near the south pole at any time.
InSight, for the whole planet only.
factors.json.Our class from volcanoes that erupted si: Our class from the volcanoes within 30 or 100 km that erupted in 1990 or later, and the nearest Holocene volcano.
factors.json.Not a hazard map and not an eruption for: It is not a hazard map, and it is not a forecast of eruptions.
The Moon has no active volcanism.
We know of no active volcanism on Mars today.
factors.json.Straight-line distance to the nearest ai: The straight-line distance to the nearest airfield, and to the nearest airfield with scheduled flights.
It is a straight-line distance, not a travel time.
factors.json.Our class from settlements, main roads a: Our class from the settlements, main roads and airfields near the area, and the people in listed settlements within 100 km.
factors.json.Not a population map: settlements under: It is not a population map. The lists do not include stations or settlements of less than 1,000 people.
factors.json.Straight-line distance to the nearest li: The straight-line distance to the nearest listed settlement and to the nearest city of 50,000 people or more.
factors.json.Not travel time; 'no settlement within 1: It is not a travel time. The words 'no settlement within 100 km' do not mean that nobody lives there.
factors.json.Our classes for solar panels, wind at 50: Our classes for solar panels, for wind at 50 m and for geothermal plants near the area.
factors.json.Not a power-yield figure for any real sy: It does not give the power output of a real system.
The lit share of the lunar region.
The sunlight on Mars, from the fact sheet.
factors.json.Who owns or governs the ground at the ar: Who owns or governs the ground at the centre of the area, and if a protected area is there. It also tells whom to ask for a permit. Some classes come from open maps, and the other classes come from territory rules.
factors.json.Not legal advice. We test the centre of: It is not legal advice. We test only the centre of the area. A territory rule is a rough guide, not a land survey. Each map covers only its own region.
factors.json.Natural Earth boundaries give the territ: Natural Earth boundaries give the territory, and official pages give each territory rule. If a polygon on an open map of protected areas or owners contains the centre, that map sets the class.
factors.json.Not applicable: no lunar land status is: Not applicable. Our data has no land status for the Moon.
factors.json.The same territory rules and maps for th: The same territory rules and maps, used for the Mars squares on Earth where a map covers the square.
factors.json.Surface pressure at night about 3 x 10^-: The surface pressure at night is approximately 3 x 10^-15 bar. There is no air, no wind, no sound and no weather.
factors.json.strong shallow moonquakes possible in th: Strong shallow moonquakes are possible in the south-polar region. There is no local count.
factors.json.Not filled tonight: no lunar albedo file: We did not fill this figure for this version of the page. We did not read a lunar albedo file, and the Moon cards do not have one. We did not write a value from memory.
factors.json.The strongest shallow moonquake recorded: The strongest shallow moonquake that the Apollo seismometers recorded (1969-1977) had its epicentre in the south-polar region. Its exact place is not known. The area of possible epicentres covers many Artemis III candidate regions. Young thrust-fault scarps are near some of these regions, and in some of them. There is no published count or rate for this lunar region. No seismometer worked near the south pole at any time.
factors.json.The same band of Sun heights is counted: The page counts the same band of Sun heights at each area on Earth.
factors.json.None expected: no wind and no liquid wat: We expect none, because there is no wind and no liquid water. New impact craters and rare slides on slopes are the only known changes. The NASA south-pole release of 2024 says that a light seismic motion can make some slopes slide. It names the inner walls of Shackleton and Nobile Rim 1.
factors.json.Not filled tonight. Diviner publishes so: We did not fill this figure for this version of the page. Diviner publishes the south-polar temperatures by local time. It gives 96 tables for each season, each of approximately 210 MB. These tables were too large to read for this version.
factors.json.No public Diviner thermal-inertia figure: We did not find a public Diviner figure for thermal inertia at the poles. The only polar (pols/poln) products in the bundle are dgdr_tbol_avg_poln, dgdr_tbol_avg_pols, pcp_avg_tbol_poln and pcp_avg_tbol_pols (bolometric temperatures). The cylindrical maps stop at 80 deg.
factors.json.One minus the mean lit share: all time,: One minus the mean lit share. It is for all time, not only for the spells of low Sun.
factors.json.3 to 5 cm (dug by the lander's arm): 3 to 5 cm (from a trench that the arm of the lander dug)
factors.json.close to the surface (published words);: close to the surface (published words). A layer that contains ice reaches 15 to >100 m.
factors.json.under less than 2 m of debris, or under: below less than 2 m of debris, or below metres of porous material (two published values)
factors.json.1,319 marsquakes heard planet-wide by In: InSight recorded 1,319 marsquakes on the whole planet. None had its location at this site.
factors.json.active dunes, about 1 m per year: active dunes that move approximately 1 m per year
factors.json.The PDS product leaves this 5 deg bin bl: The PDS product leaves this 5 deg bin blank (9999.999, 'not applicable'). It does the same for the other high-latitude bins that we checked (62.5 and 67.5 N). This map gives no value at this site. The Phoenix lander dug down to ice (see ice_depth).
factors.json.No public figure found. Jezero (18.4 N): We did not find a public figure. Jezero (18.4 N) is in the SWIM study area, but the SWIM map files did not answer when we asked. Fig. 1a of the paper puts the theoretical 3 m zone of ice stability far nearer the pole than the site.
factors.json.No public figure found. Gale (4.6 S) is: We did not find a public figure. Gale (4.6 S) is south of the SWIM study area (equator to 60 N). We did not find a map of ice depth for it.
factors.json.Measured by digging at the site: the pap: The lander measured it when it dug at the site. The abstract of the paper gives '3-5 cm deep icy soil interfaces' in the trenches. The NASA photojournal for the Dodo-Goldilocks trench (dug 12 June 2008, 7 to 8 cm deep) shows white material in its upper part. Later, scientists found that this material was ice.
factors.json.No single depth is published. SWIM's own: There is no published single depth. The SWIM map files (swim.psi.edu) did not answer when we asked (HTTP 523). Thus, we read no value at the coordinates of the site.
factors.json.No single depth is published. SWIM's map: There is no published single depth. The SWIM map files did not answer when we asked (HTTP 523).
factors.json.InSight's single seismometer, at Elysium: The single seismometer of InSight, at Elysium Planitia, detected 1,319 marsquakes during its mission. This is a count for the whole planet from one place, not a count at this site. We did not read a public catalogue of quake locations near this site for this version of the page.
factors.json.Not filled tonight. the TES rock-abundan: We did not fill this figure for this version of the page. We did not find the TES map of rock abundance (Nowicki & Christensen 2007) as a download. We did not read numbers from the colours of the map.
factors.json.No published record of dune movement or: We did not open a published record of dune movement or slope streaks at this site for this version of the page. The JPL news pages refused requests from our scripts (HTTP 403). The value is empty, not zero.
factors.json.The Bagnold Dunes on Mount Sharp's north: The Bagnold Dunes on the northwestern side of Mount Sharp, in Gale crater, are active. The wind moves Namib Dune forward by approximately one meter a year. This is the dune field near the route of the rover, not the landing point.
factors.json.Research on a national wildlife refuge m: If the Service does not take part in the research, research on a national wildlife refuge must have a Special Use Permit. PAD-US gives the public access as restricted (RA): a special permit or a registration is necessary.
factors.json.5 x 5 deg bin centred 17.5 N, 77.5 E (ab: A 5 x 5 deg bin with its centre at 17.5 N, 77.5 E (approximately 300 km wide), after a 10 deg box-car smoothing. One sigma is 0.363 wt %. The instrument senses approximately the top few tens of centimetres. This is a coarse value for the region, not a figure at the site.
factors.json.Pixel of 2.96 km at the site; derived fr: A pixel of 2.96 km at the site. A thermal model calculated it from TES night-time surface temperatures. In a 0.5 deg box around the site, the median is 102.0 and the range is 62.0 to 233.0. It is a map pixel, not a measurement on the ground at the landing point.
factors.json.Confirmed: the Diviner rock-abundance ma: We made sure that the Diviner map of rock abundance covers only the latitudes -80 to 80 deg (label MINIMUM/MAXIMUM_LATITUDE). The centre of this lunar region is at -85.99 deg, nearer the pole than the edge of the map. Thus, Diviner gives no rock abundance here. We did not find another public map of rock abundance for the lunar poles.
factors.json.5 x 5 deg bin centred 37.5 N, 22.5 E (ab: A 5 x 5 deg bin with its centre at 37.5 N, 22.5 E (approximately 300 km wide), after a 10 deg box-car smoothing. One sigma is 0.35 wt %. The instrument senses approximately the top few tens of centimetres. This is a coarse value for the region, not a figure at the site.
factors.json.Confirmed: the Diviner rock-abundance ma: We made sure that the Diviner map of rock abundance covers only the latitudes -80 to 80 deg (label MINIMUM/MAXIMUM_LATITUDE). The centre of this lunar region is at -89.46 deg, nearer the pole than the edge of the map. Thus, Diviner gives no rock abundance here. We did not find another public map of rock abundance for the lunar poles.
factors.json.Half-degree bin holding the region centr: The value is for the half-degree bin that holds the centre of the lunar region. The 264 bins with centres in the lunar region have values from 143.8 to 147.4 ppm. The instrument cannot tell the difference between ice in a cold trap and hydrogen that is mixed through the soil.
factors.json.5 x 5 deg bin centred 37.5 N, 192.5 E (a: A 5 x 5 deg bin with its centre at 37.5 N, 192.5 E (approximately 300 km wide), after a 10 deg box-car smoothing. One sigma is 0.426 wt %. The instrument senses approximately the top few tens of centimetres. This is a coarse value for the region, not a figure at the site.
factors.json.Half-degree bin holding the region centr: The value is for the half-degree bin that holds the centre of the lunar region. The 48 bins with centres in the lunar region have values from 122.8 to 143.0 ppm. The instrument cannot tell the difference between ice in a cold trap and hydrogen that is mixed through the soil.
factors.json.Entry into an Antarctic Specially Protec: To go into an Antarctic Specially Protected Area, you must have a permit from an appropriate national authority (Annex V, Articles 3 and 7).
factors.json.Half-degree bin holding the region centr: The value is for the half-degree bin that holds the centre of the lunar region. The 56 bins with centres in the lunar region have values from 120.9 to 151.9 ppm. The instrument cannot tell the difference between ice in a cold trap and hydrogen that is mixed through the soil.
factors.json.Pixel of 2.96 km at the site; derived fr: A pixel of 2.96 km at the site. A thermal model calculated it from TES night-time surface temperatures. In a 0.5 deg box around the site, the median is 349.0 and the range is 237.0 to 457.0. It is a map pixel, not a measurement on the ground at the landing point.
factors.json.Confirmed: the Diviner rock-abundance ma: We made sure that the Diviner map of rock abundance covers only the latitudes -80 to 80 deg (label MINIMUM/MAXIMUM_LATITUDE). The centre of this lunar region is at -85.43 deg, nearer the pole than the edge of the map. Thus, Diviner gives no rock abundance here. We did not find another public map of rock abundance for the lunar poles.
factors.json.The Government of Yukon site refused our: The Government of Yukon site refused our requests. Thus, we did not read its licence pages. Find the permit authority before field work. On Settlement Land, the Yukon First Nation holds the rights of an owner.
Ground surface: the daily swing is 77.0 to 102.0 K over the year, with a mean of 91.6 K. Air at 2 m: the mean is 54.5 K, and the largest is 62.9 K. These are model values on the MCD grid, at intervals of 1 hour. They are not measurements.
factors.json.Entry into an Antarctic Specially Manage: A permit is not necessary to go into an Antarctic Specially Managed Area. But a permit is necessary to go into an ASPA in it (Annex V, Article 4).
factors.json.To leave a 17(b) easement and go onto Na: If you leave a 17(b) easement and go onto Native land without permission from the owner, this is trespass. PAD-US gives the public access as open (OA).

factors.json.Greenland has joint ownership of land, s: Greenland has joint ownership of land. Thus, nobody can buy or sell land. A person or a company gets a right of use through an area allotment. factors.json.Half-degree bin holding the region centr: The value is for the half-degree bin that holds the centre of the lunar region. factors.json.Find the manager or the owner of the lan: Find the manager or the owner of the land on a map. Ask that body before field work. Research on National Park Service or Fish and Wildlife Service land must have a permit.
factors.json.Alaska is a mix of federal land, State o: Alaska is a mix of federal land, State of Alaska land, Alaska Native Corporation land and other private land. extra-prose.json.Daily panel yield per kilowatt of panels: The daily panel yield for each kilowatt of panels is the daily sunlight on level ground, in kWh per square metre, multiplied by 0.75.
extra-prose.json.A panel rating assumes 1 kW of sunlight: The rating of a panel assumes 1 kW of sunlight per square metre. The factor 0.75 includes the losses from heat, dirt, snow, wires and the inverter.
extra-prose.json.Panels tilted toward a low Sun can do be: Panels that are tilted toward a low Sun can give more power. This estimate does not include that increase.
extra-prose.json.Solar is good at a yearly mean of at lea: If the yearly mean is at least 4.5 kWh per square metre per day, solar is good. That is approximately 1,640 kWh per square metre in a year.
extra-prose.json.Central Europe gives about 3 kWh per squ: Central Europe gives approximately 3 kWh per square metre per day. The high Arctic gives approximately 2.
extra-prose.json.A month has no Sun only when NASA POWER: A month has no Sun only if NASA POWER gives exactly 0.0 for it. If a month is blank, it is unknown, not dark.
extra-prose.json.The yearly mean is the plain mean of the: The yearly mean is the simple mean of the 12 monthly means. It includes direct and diffuse sunlight.
extra-prose.json.Sunlight comes from NASA POWER ALLSKY_SF: Sunlight comes from NASA POWER ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN and CERES SYN1deg. The monthly means are for the years of the service and for the 1-degree box that contains the area.
extra-prose.json.A panel facing a low Sun: A panel that faces a low Sun
extra-prose.json.Sunlight above the air is 1,361 watts pe: Above the air, the sunlight is 1,361 watts per square metre at Earth and at the Moon. This value comes from the NASA NSSDCA fact sheets.
extra-prose.json.An upright lunar panel facing a Sun on t: On the Moon, a vertical panel that faces a Sun on the horizon gets all of that beam. There is no air to make it less bright.
extra-prose.json.Air mass describes the thickness of air: Air mass is the thickness of air that the sunlight goes through, compared with a Sun directly overhead. The Sun height h is in degrees.
extra-prose.json.The sea-level formula is AM = 1 / (sin h: The formula for sea level is AM = 1 / (sin h + 0.50572 × (h + 6.07995)^−1.6364). It does not include the height of the area.
extra-prose.json.This formula comes from Applied Solar En: This formula comes from Applied Solar Energy (1976), as PVEducation quotes it. One air mass of typical clear air lets a share of 0.7 through.
extra-prose.json.Lunar Sun ceilings are 2.08, 5.55, 6.11: The Sun ceilings of the lunar regions are 2.08, 5.55, 6.11 and 7.59 degrees. We calculate the power at each ceiling and at half of that height.
extra-prose.json.Much of the time, the Sun is below its c: During many of the hours of low Sun, the Sun is below its ceiling.
extra-prose.json.For each best ten-day period, the clear: For each best ten-day period, the clear share is 1 − cloud percent / 100. We give each period a weight by its hours of low Sun.
extra-prose.json.We average those shares over the months: We calculate the mean of those shares over the months of the best periods. The periods come from the low-Sun data for each lunar region.
extra-prose.json.Cloud comes from CERES SYN1deg monthly m: The cloud figures are CERES SYN1deg monthly means over all hours. The low-Sun power under a typical sky is the clear-air power multiplied by that clear share.
extra-prose.json.The typical-sky figure is unknown when c: If the cloud is unknown, the figure for a typical sky is unknown. It is also unknown if the area has no best periods for that lunar region.
extra-prose.json.Standard sea-level air density is 1.225: The standard air density at sea level is 1.225 kilograms per cubic metre. We use the International Standard Atmosphere.
extra-prose.json.Height is the mean elevation of the mode: The height z is the mean height of the model box that holds the 50 m wind. If there is no height, we use the density at sea level.
If the height of the model box is unknown, it stays unknown. Cold polar air can be approximately 10% denser at −15 °C. The figure does not include this increase.
extra-prose.json.The usual wind-speed spread gives mean s: For the usual spread of wind speeds, the mean of the speed cubed is 6 / pi times the mean speed cubed. Rounded, this factor is 1.91.
extra-prose.json.Power in wind at 50 m = 0.5 × air densit: Power in wind at 50 m = 0.5 × air density × 1.91 × (yearly mean speed)^3. The units are watts per square metre of rotor area.
extra-prose.json.This is power carried by moving air. A t: This is the power that the wind carries. A turbine takes a maximum of 59%, and in practice 35% to 45%.
extra-prose.json.Yearly speed is the plain mean of the 12: The yearly speed is the simple mean of the 12 monthly means of NASA POWER WS50M. These means come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis.
extra-prose.json.The nearest MERRA-2 point represents a 0: The nearest MERRA-2 point is for a grid box of 0.5 by 0.625 degrees. The monthly means of wind include all hours.
extra-prose.json.These bands follow the published table a: These bands follow the published table as the author of the source knows it. Nobody saved a copy of the table with these inputs.
extra-prose.json.Wind is good from class 4 upward: at lea: Wind is good in class 4 and higher, at 400 watts per square metre or more. It is fair in classes 2 and 3.
extra-prose.json.Fair spans 200 up to 400 watts per squar: Fair is from 200 up to 400 watts per square metre. Wind is poor in class 1, below 200.
extra-prose.json.Geothermal is good when a working geothe: Geothermal is good if an active geothermal power plant is within 50 km. A volcano within 30 km that erupted in 1990 or later also gives this class.
extra-prose.json.Plants come from the WRI Global Power Pl: The plants come from the WRI Global Power Plant Database. Their primary fuel must be geothermal.
extra-prose.json.A recent volcano has a listed last erupt: A recent volcano has a listed year of last eruption of 1990 or later. A confirmed eruption that started or stopped in 1990 or later also makes a volcano recent.
extra-prose.json.Geothermal is fair when a working plant: Geothermal is fair if an active plant is within 150 km. A Holocene volcano within 100 km also gives this class.
extra-prose.json.Holocene means the last 11,700 years. Ge: Holocene means the last 11,700 years. In all other conditions, geothermal is poor.
extra-prose.json.Steady volcanic effects are likely when: Steady volcanic effects are likely if a volcano that agrees with the next rule is within 30 km of the centre of the area.
extra-prose.json.It must have erupted in at least 3 separ: That volcano must have eruptions in 3 or more separate years from 1990, or an eruption in 2015 or later.
extra-prose.json.Volcanic effects come and go when a volc: Volcanic effects come and go if a volcano that erupted in 1990 or later is within 100 km. In all other conditions, we expect no volcanic effects.
extra-prose.json.Possible effects include gas and volcani: Possible effects are gas and volcanic haze that can corrode instruments and optics, and make optics less clear. Fine ash and abrasive dust can be on the ground and in the air.
extra-prose.json.Warm or steaming ground can upset temper: Warm ground or steam can change temperature measurements. Small volcanic tremors, and closure of the area during eruptions, can also affect the work.
extra-prose.json.Young volcanic ground requires a Holocen: For young volcanic ground, a Holocene volcano within 50 km and volcanic rock on the rock map are necessary. Holocene means active in approximately the last 11,700 years.
extra-prose.json.It is false when no Holocene volcano is: It is false if no Holocene volcano is that near, or if the rock map shows rock that is not volcanic. It is unknown if a volcano is that near but the rock map gives no class.
extra-prose.json.Fresh lava and ash can represent basalt: Fresh lava and ash can represent the basalt soil of the dark plains of the Moon and of Mars.
extra-prose.json.Steady human disturbance is likely when: Steady human disturbance is likely if one of these conditions is true. One condition is a listed settlement of 1,000 people or more within 5 km.
extra-prose.json.A main road or railway within 2 km also: A main road or railway within 2 km also gives this class. An airfield with scheduled flights within 10 km also gives this class.
extra-prose.json.Human disturbance is possible with any l: Human disturbance is possible if a listed settlement of any size is within 25 km. A main road, a railway or an airfield of any type within 10 km also gives this class.
extra-prose.json.Possible effects include vehicle and air: Possible effects are vibration from vehicles and aircraft, radio noise, dust from traffic and artificial light. Tracks and litter can be in camera views.
extra-prose.json.Help is within reach with a listed settl: Help is within reach if a listed settlement of 1,000 people or more is within 50 km.
extra-prose.json.An airfield with scheduled flights withi: An airfield with scheduled flights within 100 km also gives this result. Help means possible power, shelter and rescue. In all other conditions, this flag is false.
extra-prose.json.The nearest listed settlement uses GeoNa: The nearest listed settlement comes from GeoNames cities1000. If there is no population figure, the population stays unknown.
extra-prose.json.Population within 25 km is the sum of li: The population within 25 km is the sum of the listed populations. If no settlement is listed, it is zero.
extra-prose.json.It is unknown when settlements exist but: It is unknown if there are settlements but none has a population figure. If only some figures are not available, the sum is a lower bound.
extra-prose.json.Roads and railways use Natural Earth 1:1: Roads and railways come from Natural Earth 1:10m, without ferries. If there is no road or railway within 1,000 km, the distance is unknown.
extra-prose.json.Airfields use OurAirports runway airport: Airfields come from the OurAirports list of runway airports of all sizes, with gravel and ice strips. The list does not include heliports, seaplane bases or closed fields.
extra-prose.json.Scheduled service uses the airfield list: Scheduled flights come from a flag in the airfield list. The points on a road are a maximum of 1.5 km apart. Thus, a distance to a road can be too large by a maximum of 0.75 km.
extra-prose.json.The generalised road lines can themselve: The simplified road lines can be a kilometre or more away from the real roads.
extra-prose.json.Each class is a rough estimate by our ow: Each class is a rough estimate by our own rule of thumb. If the earthquake catalogue can give a verdict, we use that verdict.
extra-prose.json.Small tremors are likely when a volcano: Small tremors are likely if a volcano that erupted in 1990 or later is within 50 km.
extra-prose.json.At least 5 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or: At least 5 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more within 200 km from 1990 also give this class.
extra-prose.json.Small tremors are possible with any Holo: Small tremors are possible if a Holocene volcano of any date is within 100 km.
extra-prose.json.One to 4 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or m: Between 1 and 4 earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more within 200 km from 1990 also give this class.
extra-prose.json.Glacier ice covering at least 10% of an: Glacier ice on 10% or more of the land of the area also gives this class. Ice that moves makes small quakes.
extra-prose.json.Small tremors are unlikely otherwise. Mi: In all other conditions, small tremors are unlikely. If the earthquake input or the glacier input is not available, the class stays unknown.
extra-prose.json.The larger-earthquake input covers 1990–: The input for larger earthquakes covers 1990–2025. Glacier ice comes from ESA WorldCover in the north and from the share of ice sheet in the south.
extra-prose.json.We keep our estimate even where the cata: We keep our estimate also where the catalogue sees small tremors. Thus, you can compare the two.
extra-prose.json.The USGS catalogue covers 2010–2025, a s: The USGS catalogue covers 2010–2025, a period of 16 years. The events have a magnitude of 1 or more and less than 5.
extra-prose.json.All magnitude types and all event types: We count all types of magnitude and all types of event. Earthquakes, quarry blasts, explosions and ice quakes can all shake instruments.
extra-prose.json.Steady small tremors require events with: For steady small tremors, events within 100 km are necessary in at least 12 of the 16 years. The rate must also be 5 or more per year.
extra-prose.json.Occasional small tremors means at least: Occasional small tremors means that there is at least one event within 100 km, but the two conditions for steady tremors are not both true.
extra-prose.json.That means events in 1 to 11 years, or f: Thus, there are events in 1 to 11 years, or fewer than 5 per year. Events in 1 to 3 years are usually one swarm.
extra-prose.json.None recorded applies when small tremors: None recorded applies if the catalogue records small tremors here but shows none within 100 km.
extra-prose.json.Cannot tell applies when the catalogue c: Cannot tell applies if the catalogue cannot see small tremors here.
extra-prose.json.It also applies when only magnitudes abo: It also applies if the catalogue sees only magnitudes above a floor between 2.5 and 3.5, and shows no event within 100 km.
extra-prose.json.An empty circle then says nothing about: In that condition, an empty circle does not tell you about smaller tremors.
extra-prose.json.The detection floor uses the 10th percen: The detection floor is the 10th percentile of the magnitudes of the events within 500 km over the 16 years. If there are fewer than 30 events, the floor is unknown.
extra-prose.json.Small tremors are recorded when the floo: If the floor is 2.5 or less, the catalogue records small tremors. If the floor is above 2.5 and not more than 3.5, the catalogue records only larger tremors.
extra-prose.json.A floor above 3.5, or too few events, me: If the floor is above 3.5, or if there are too few events, the catalogue cannot see small tremors.
extra-prose.json.A floor at most 2.5 also needs a nearby: A floor of 2.5 or less must also pass a check near the area. The catalogue must show at least one event below that floor within 200 km.
extra-prose.json.Otherwise, a better-watched network fart: If not, a better network farther away gave the low floor. Then we treat the area as a place where the catalogue cannot see small tremors.
extra-prose.json.Examples include western Alaska viewed f: Examples are western Alaska, seen from Chukotka, and Texas, seen from Coahuila.
extra-prose.json.Where small tremors cannot be seen, thei: Where the catalogue cannot see small tremors, their counts are unknown, never zero. If there is no record, there can still be tremors.
extra-prose.json.Larger events listed anyway within 100 k: If the catalogue still lists larger events within 100 km, they show some activity. Their count is a lower bound, never a rate of small tremors.
extra-prose.json.Duplicate events across catalogue reques: If two catalogue requests give the same event, we keep it only one time, by its event ID.
extra-prose.json.Requests cover polar latitudes from 55 t: The requests cover the latitudes from 55 to 90 degrees in each hemisphere. In the north, each request covers one month. In the south, each request covers one year.
extra-prose.json.Answers exceeding 20,000 events are requ: If an answer has more than 20,000 events, we request it again by month, then by halves of longitude.
extra-prose.json.Distances, unknowns and source collectio: Distances, unknown values and data collection
extra-prose.json.Distances run from the area centre along: Distances go from the centre of the area along a great circle. The source uses a sphere for the Earth, with a radius of 6,371.0088 km.
extra-prose.json.Areas are about 11 km across. Any point: Areas are approximately 11 km wide. A point in the area can be approximately 8 km nearer or farther than the distance from the centre.
extra-prose.json.Unknown is stored as null, never zero. A: The data stores unknown as null, never as zero. A count of zero means that the list has no entries in the stated radius.
extra-prose.json.Nearest-feature searches expand until th: The search for the nearest feature goes farther until it finds a match. For roads and railways, the search stops at 1,000 km.
extra-prose.json.The source collection asks NASA POWER on: The collection of the source data sends one request at a time to NASA POWER, with at least 2 seconds between requests.
extra-prose.json.After a refusal (429) or server fault (5: After a refusal (429) or a server fault (5xx), the collection waits for at least one minute.
extra-prose.json.After a dropped connection, collection w: After a lost connection, the collection waits 20, 40, 60 seconds and more, to a maximum of 300 seconds. Then it tries again.
extra-prose.json.These are source collection rules. This: These are the rules for the collection of the source data. This page reads only its local exported data.
extra-prose.json.This is not a measurement at the area. I: This is not a measurement at the area. It is not the yield of a tilted panel, or of a panel that follows the Sun.
extra-prose.json.It includes daylight beyond the low-Sun: It includes the daylight outside the hours of low Sun. At these latitudes, the coarse box is approximately 111 km by 20 to 55 km.
extra-prose.json.This is a textbook clear-air estimate, n: This is a textbook estimate for clear air, not a measurement. It does not include diffuse light from the sky.
extra-prose.json.Real polar air changes with haze, ice cr: Real polar air changes with haze, ice crystals and aerosols. A real panel can get less power, or a little more.
extra-prose.json.Cloud is a monthly mean over all hours,: The cloud figure is a monthly mean over all hours, not only the hours of low Sun. Its box is approximately 111 km tall.
extra-prose.json.Earth's low Sun delivers only a fraction: On Earth, the low Sun gives only a part of the power that a panel gets under the same low Sun on the Moon.
On the Moon, no air stops the light.
extra-prose.json.This is a coarse grid mean, not a measur: This is a mean for a coarse grid box, not a measurement at the area. The box is approximately 55 km by 20 to 35 km.
extra-prose.json.Hills, coasts, valleys, downslope ice wi: Hills, coasts, valleys, cold winds that flow down from ice, and ice on the blades can change the conditions very much. This is not the power that a turbine gives.
extra-prose.json.Nobody has drilled or measured heat here: Nobody drilled here or measured the heat here. This only shows that hot rock is possibly near the surface.
extra-prose.json.Areas far from volcanoes can have useful: Areas far from volcanoes can have useful warm ground, for example deep basins and hot springs. Areas near volcanoes can have ground that is not usable.
extra-prose.json.The source could not fetch an open world: The source did not get an open world map of geothermal potential, because a login was necessary. The list of plants stops at approximately 2021 and does not include some plants.
extra-prose.json.This is not a hazard map or eruption for: This is not a hazard map or a forecast of eruptions. One point at the summit or at the centre of the field represents each volcano.
extra-prose.json.A fissure system or volcanic field can e: A fissure system or a volcanic field can go far beyond that point. Gas and ash can move with the wind much farther than 100 km.
extra-prose.json.Years erupting means calendar years with: The years with eruptions are the calendar years in which a confirmed eruption continued. If an eruption has no end year, we count only its start year.
extra-prose.json.Uncertain and discredited eruptions are: We do not include uncertain or discredited eruptions. We do not count lava lakes or steady gas release between listed eruptions.
extra-prose.json.This is not a population map, or a noise: This is not a population map, and it is not a measurement of noise or light. Distances are straight-line distances, not travel distances.
extra-prose.json.GeoNames cities1000 lists settlements ab: GeoNames cities1000 lists settlements of more than 1,000 people and seats of local government. Camps, stations, mines and hamlets are possibly not in the list.
extra-prose.json.Natural Earth lists only main roads and: Natural Earth lists only main roads and railways. Most tracks, winter roads and mine roads are not in it.
If the list shows no road, there can still be a road. We know that each airfield exists, but we do not know its traffic.
extra-prose.json.Our estimate is not a tremor count or me: Our estimate is not a count or a measurement of tremors. It is a guess from active volcanoes, larger earthquakes and glaciers that move.
extra-prose.json.Small tremors can occur where they seem: Small tremors can occur where our estimate says unlikely. Where it says likely, they possibly do not occur.
extra-prose.json.These are catalogued events, not ground-: These are catalogued events, not measurements of ground motion at the area. This is not a hazard map. Only a seismometer at the place gives a real test.
extra-prose.json.The catalogue sees only what nearby inst: The catalogue contains only the events that nearby instruments detect. In Alaska, it records magnitude 1 to 2.
extra-prose.json.The remote Arctic, Siberia and Antarctic: In the remote Arctic, Siberia and Antarctica, it records almost nothing below magnitude 4.
extra-prose.json.Networks grew during the 16 years. North: The networks increased during the 16 years. North of 55° N, the yearly counts of magnitude 1–5 in 2017–2025 were approximately 1.6 times the counts in 2010–2015.
extra-prose.json.Some areas, including the Kobuk valley,: Some areas, for example the Kobuk valley, recorded several times as many. Thus, the early years show too few events, and the number of years with events can be too low.
extra-prose.json.Distances run from the area centre. Even: Distances go from the centre of the area. We got the events from 55 degrees to the pole.
extra-prose.json.For areas at 59 to about 59.5° N, the 50: For areas at 59 to approximately 59.5° N, the 500 km circle goes a little south of 55° N.
extra-prose.json.Their detection floor therefore uses sli: Thus, the detection floor for these areas uses slightly fewer events.
extra-prose.json.A panel facing the Sun receives 1,361 wa: A panel that faces the Sun gets 1,361 watts per square metre at all times when the Sun is above the local horizon. There is no atmosphere.
extra-prose.json.Source: NASA Goddard average solar illum: Source: NASA Goddard average solar illumination map, PGDA product 69. It uses intervals of 1 hour over 18.6 years on LOLA terrain.
extra-prose.json.The fact sheet gives surface pressure as: The fact sheet gives the surface pressure as 3 × 10^−15 bar. The total mass of the atmosphere is 25,000 kg.
extra-prose.json.Sunlight above the air is 586.2 watts pe: Above the air, the sunlight is 586.2 watts per square metre, a share of 0.431 of the value for Earth.
During the Mars year, it changes from 490.3 to 713.3 watts per square metre. Source: NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet.
extra-prose.json.Dust stays in the sky all year. Optical: Dust stays in the sky all year. The optical depth is usually below 1 during the aphelion season, Ls 0–180.
extra-prose.json.It exceeds 3 at the peak of global dust: It is more than 3 at the peak of global dust storms. These figures come from observations by 7 landers.
extra-prose.json.For Earth, the source recalls a global m: For Earth, the source gives from memory a global mean optical depth of approximately 0.1–0.2 at 550 nm. Nobody checked that figure for Earth.
extra-prose.json.Yearly mean model pressure ranges from 4: The yearly mean pressure in the model is from 480 to 896 Pa at the 57 Mars sites. On Earth at sea level, it is 101,325 Pa.
extra-prose.json.At the same wind speed, Mars carries a s: At the same wind speed, the wind on Mars carries a share of 0.0131 of the wind power on Earth. This share is the ratio of the air densities.
